correctness.rationale: The curve-Hessian restriction is \(H|_C=54x\Phi_r(y)\), and exact identities \(\operatorname{disc}(P_r)=3(r^2-4)D(r)\) and \(\operatorname{Res}(P_r,u^2+ru+1)=16(r^2-4)^2\) give the four branch flexes, eighteen residual ordinary flexes, and the double hyperflex at infinity on the stated generic open. Frobenius on cubic-root fibers yields three exhaustive cases. Independent direct enumeration over \(\mathbb F_7\), \(\mathbb F_{49}\), and \(\mathbb F_{343}\) agrees with the complete finite-field table; the algebraic argument, not finite experiments, proves the uniform statement.

value.rationale: The canonical quartic’s flex-support scheme is an intrinsic finite arithmetic invariant. Its full extension-degree splitting refines geometric hyperflex counts, and over \(\mathbb F_7\) it separates quadratic twists with identical rational flex numbers. The general formula requires only degree-four/six factoring and cubic-residue tests and determines all finite-extension point counts of the support. The generic-open restriction is natural and intrinsic to the geometric jump discriminant, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
